methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $300K total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Hedral is a seed-stage company in the Housing & Construction sector founded by Arjo Mozumder. The analysis draws on a private peer set of five companies—BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Unlimited Industries, Ground Control Development, and ADMARES—as no public comparables exist in this specific frontier-tech construction subsector.

The Stage-Progression method is applicable and forms the sole quantitative input to this valuation. Using total capital raised of $300K as a proxy for seed-stage valuation, the analysis applies a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to reflect progression to the next funding stage. This yields an implied value of $750K. The triangulation range, derived from this single method with conservative and optimistic variance bounds, spans from $638K (low) to $862K (high), with a median point estimate of $750K.

The analysis supports a median valuation of approximately $750K, with a plausible range of $638K to $862K. Key limitations include reliance on a single methodology and the absence of comparable public market anchors. The valuation remains highly sensitive to revised assumptions about stage-progression multiples specific to frontier construction technology, as well as to future capital raises and revenue traction that would enable revenue or market-size-based approaches. Additional data on peer financials and Hedral's technical progress would materially refine this range.
